subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 9: India's Long Road to Independence
central_question: How did diverse Indians, using different ideas and methods, turn resistance to colonial rule into a broad national struggle that ended in independence and Partition?
in_scope_units: British Crown rule after the Great Uprising, colonial discrimination and continuing economic exploitation
Reform movements and cultural influences that contributed to national awakening
The rise of the Indian National Congress and early political demands
Growing discontent, the Partition of Bengal, Swadeshi, boycott and the Nationalist agenda
The All-India Muslim League, the Surat split and debates over political strategy
Revolutionary organisations and armed resistance, including the Ghadar Movement
Home Rule, the Lucknow Pact and Gandhi’s emergence through satyagraha
Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh, Non-Cooperation and the Khilafat alliance
Simon Commission, revolutionary action, Purna Swaraj and Civil Disobedience
Gandhi-Irwin Pact, debates over representation and the Poona Pact
World War II, Subhas Chandra Bose, the INA and Quit India
End of British authority, communal conflict, the Cabinet Mission, Independence and Partition
banned_topics: A detailed retelling of the Great Uprising of 1857 already covered in the previous textbook part
Post-independence nation-building beyond the immediate transition of 1947
Biographical details about leaders that are not supplied in the chapter

known_pitfalls.claim: The Indian National Congress demanded complete independence from the moment it was founded.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter distinguishes the early Congress approach from the later demand for Swaraj and eventually Purna Swaraj.

known_pitfalls.claim: All freedom fighters agreed on one method for ending British rule.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter repeatedly shows disagreements among Moderates, Nationalists, revolutionaries, Gandhians and other political groups even though they opposed colonial domination.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Non-Cooperation Movement and the Civil Disobedience Movement were the same campaign.
known_pitfalls.correction: They were separate mass movements launched in different contexts; Civil Disobedience began with the Salt March after the demand for Purna Swaraj.

known_pitfalls.claim: Independence in 1947 occurred without a major political and human cost.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter ends with Independence alongside Partition, communal violence and mass displacement.

recommended_example_progression: Questions and activities, True or False 1: test whether the Congress demanded independence from its inception
Questions and activities, “Who Am I?” 2: identify Tilak through Swaraj, Kesari and public festivals
Questions and activities on peasants, workers, tribals and students: compare forms of participation in the national movement
Questions and activities on Nehru’s 15 August 1947 speech: interpret “redeem our pledge” and the “soul of a nation”
Questions and activities, freedom-fighter task: justify a method for achieving freedom using evidence from the chapter
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with “Questions and activities”, including True or False, “Who Am I?”, source interpretation and extended discussion or role-based tasks.
